subject.title: [security] Tencent Cloud redirects can disclose session tokens and cloud-init credentials

question: Should Tencent Cloud requests fail closed on every redirect that changes the initiating request’s scheme, canonical host, or effective port, while preserving caller-supplied stricter redirect policies?
rationale: This is a security-boundary and upgrade-compatibility choice: a same-origin-only policy prevents credential and cloud-init replay, but may intentionally stop any existing provider endpoint redirect workflow.

options.title: Adopt origin-confined redirects
options.body: Clone the client and allow only redirects that retain the initiating origin’s HTTPS scheme, canonical hostname, and effective port, with focused compatibility tests.

options.title: Retain Go defaults with documented caveat
options.body: Accept the redirect exposure precondition and keep default redirect following, documenting that operators must supply a strict client policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt origin-confined redirects
recommendation.body: Clone the client and allow only redirects that retain the initiating origin’s HTTPS scheme, canonical hostname, and effective port, with focused compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter supplied the concrete reproduction and policy proposal; a repository security/code owner should make the final boundary decision.
